No, that's outside assembly, in the return lines. `0x0100 ** (...)` — exponent with hex literal ok? `**` with literals fine. `~` on uint fine. But `abi.encodePacked(0x20, length)` — 0x20 is uint256? literal fine.

Fix assembly else: use switch or two ifs.

Also `data` unused? used. `if (!(0x1f & length))` — fine.

Rewrite assembly:

if and(packed, 0x1) {
    length := shr(1, packed)
    data := shr(8, packed)
}
if iszero(and(packed, 1)) {
    length := sload(add(slot,1))
    data := sload(add(slot,2))
}

Also `shr(0x1, packed)` shift literal must be constant? shr takes any value, fine.

Also `~(0x0100 ** (0x20 - (0x1f & length)) - 0x01)` — 0x1f & length: literal & variable ok. Exponentiation 0x0100 ** uint — literal**expr: 0x0100 is rational literal? hex literal is int? Actually 0x0100 without size... hex number literal is fine, converts. But `0x20 - (0x1f & length)` — 0x20 literal minus uint256 ok. Result type: literal expression may be fine. To be safe cast: `uint256(0x1) << ...`? Keep minimal; likely compiles. Actually `0x0100 ** x` where x uint256 — literal ** uint256: allowed, type is uint256? Literal exponentiation: both literals -> rational; literal ** uint256 -> uint256? I think yes. Then `~(... - 0x01)` fine, `& data` fine.

But `abi.encodePacked(0x20, length, ...)` mixing — fine.
